Use of Geothermal Energy as a Renewable Source of Energy with the Help of Heat Pumps
abstract: Geothermal heat pumps are widely used for heating and cooling buildings. This technology is based on the principle of heat transfer between the ground and the building, significantly reducing electricity or fossil fuel consumption. In winter, heat from the ground is transferred to the building, and in summer, excess heat is returned to the ground. This closed-loop system not only provides a comfortable microclimate but also saves up to 50-70% of energy compared to traditional heating methods. This article discusses the operating principles, key technological solutions, as well as the environmental and economic aspects of using such systems. The focus is on heat transfer system types: vertical ground probes, horizontal collectors, and groundwater-based systems. Factors influencing configuration selection are analyzed, including geological conditions, available space, and the facility's heat load. It is emphasized that proper circuit calculation and design are key to long-term and efficient system operation. In conclusion, it is argued that integrating geothermal heat pumps into the energy systems of buildings and residential areas is a promising approach to decarbonizing heat supply, increasing energy independence, and achieving sustainable development goals. The widespread adoption of this technology will be facilitated by the development of a regulatory framework, government support, and increased awareness of its benefits.

title: The influence of workload and work stress on performance mediated by burnout at the Samarinda post office
abstract: This study examines the effects of workload and work stress on employee performance, with burnout as a mediating variable, among employees of the Samarinda Post Office. A quantitative explanatory research design was employed, involving 64 employees selected through a census sampling technique. Data were collected from January to March 2026 using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings indicate that workload (β = −0.356; p = 0.008) and work stress (β = −0.317; p < 0.001) have negative and significant relationships with employee performance. Both workload (β = 0.446; p = 0.037) and work stress (β = 0.422; p = 0.036) have positive and significant relationships with burnout. Furthermore, burnout has a negative and significant relationship with employee performance (β = −0.311; p = 0.014). The mediation analysis shows that burnout significantly mediates the relationship between workload and employee performance (β = −0.138; p = 0.047), whereas its mediating effect on the relationship between work stress and employee performance is not significant (β = −0.131; p = 0.142). These findings suggest that workload, work stress, and burnout are important factors associated with employee performance. The study also highlights that burnout may explain the workload–performance relationship, but does not statistically explain the work stress–performance relationship in the observed sample.

title: The Influence of Sales Promotion Content, Content Attractiveness, and User-Friendliness on Financial Decision Making through Imitation Intention
abstract: Purpose: This study examines the influence of sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness on financial decision making through imitation intention among social media users in Indonesia, particularly in the context of influencer marketing for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the food and beverage sector. Research Method: This study uses a quantitative explanatory design with a cross-sectional approach. Data are collected through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale and purposive sampling. Data analysis employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS. Results and Discussion: The study proposes that sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness influence imitation intention and financial decision making. Imitation intention is also expected to influence financial decision making and mediate the relationships between promotional content characteristics and financial decisions. These relationships will be evaluated empirically. Implications: The findings are expected to help MSMEs and influencers develop promotional strategies that encourage informed financial decisions among social media users. Future research may examine other factors affecting consumer financial behavior. Originality: This study integrates three influencer promotional content characteristics with imitation intention to explain financial decision making in the Indonesian MSME food and beverage sector.

title: Multi-tiered Reading Comprehension Interventions and Home-school Partnerships Across grade 6 Learners
journal: The International Review of Multidisciplinary Research
abstract: This descriptive-developmental study assessed multi-tiered reading comprehension interventions and home-school partnerships among Grade 6 learners at Canjulao, Lo-ok, and Timpolok Elementary Schools in District 7, Schools Division of Lapu-Lapu City, during School Year 2026–2027. It aimed to establish an empirical basis for an Integrated Literacy Development Plan. Using purposive stratified sampling, the study involved 99 respondents: nine intermediate English teachers, 45 parents or guardians, and 45 struggling readers. Data from content-validated four-point Likert questionnaires were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, weighted means, and standard deviations. Diagnostic results showed that 73.33% of learner-respondents performed at the Philippine Informal Reading Inventory Frustration level in English silent reading comprehension. Implementation declined across successive intervention tiers. Tier 1 universal instruction registered a high composite mean of 2.97, although differentiated texts were insufficient (2.39). Tier 2 small-group guided reading achieved a marginally high mean of 2.57, constrained by scheduling disruptions (2.28) and inadequate leveled reading kits (2.23). Tier 3 intensive remediation scored low (2.00), reflecting limited individualized remediation plans (1.98) and one-on-one diagnostic tutoring (1.87). Home-school partnerships also showed low implementation (2.42). Although bilingual communication channels were functional (2.85), weaknesses persisted in home literacy environments (2.30), comprehension support at home (2.37), and community collaboration (2.18). Major barriers included excessive screen time and gaming (81.82%), irregular parental work schedules (77.78%), insufficient remedial reading materials (75.76%), and teachers’ administrative workloads (71.72%). In response, the study developed Project READ-ALIGN (Reading Empowerment through Aligned Interventions and Domestic-School Networks), a ten-point program combining tiered instructional guides, bilingual home literacy toolkits, and barangay-based literacy collaboration. The proposed initiative seeks to strengthen individualized instruction, improve parental participation, coordinate community support, and promote sustained reading comprehension development among struggling learners. It further emphasizes consistent progress monitoring, accessible instructional resources, manageable intervention schedules, and shared accountability among teachers, families, and community stakeholders for literacy improvement.
